claim: Sox17 is a key transcriptional regulator of definitive endoderm development.
source: Sox17 is a key transcriptional regulator of definitive endoderm development, and yet, its genomic targets remain largely uncharacterized.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about Sox17's role.

claim: Sox17 functionally interacts with the canonical Wnt pathway to specify and pattern the endoderm while repressing alternative mesectoderm fates.
source: We show that Sox17 functionally interacts with the canonical Wnt pathway to specify and pattern the endoderm while repressing alternative mesectoderm fates.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by the genomic approaches and epistasis experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Sox17 and β-catenin co-occupy hundreds of key enhancers.
source: Sox17 and β-catenin co-occupy hundreds of key enhancers.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data showing 3956 genomic loci co-occupied by both Sox17 and Bcat.

claim: Sox17 and β-catenin synergistically activate transcription apparently independent of Tcfs on some enhancers.
source: In some cases, Sox17 and β-catenin synergistically activate transcription apparently independent of Tcfs, whereas on other enhancers, Sox17 represses β-catenin/Tcf-mediated transcription to spatially restrict gene expression domains.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by luciferase reporter assays showing synergistic activation of six1, osr1, and igf3 enhancers.

claim: Sox17 represses β-catenin/Tcf-mediated transcription on some enhancers to spatially restrict gene expression domains.
source: In some cases, Sox17 and β-catenin synergistically activate transcription apparently independent of Tcfs, whereas on other enhancers, Sox17 represses β-catenin/Tcf-mediated transcription to spatially restrict gene expression domains.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by luciferase reporter assays showing Sox17 repression of dkk1 and lhx5 enhancers.

claim: In Xenopus, there are three redundant sox17 genes: sox17a, sox17b.1 and sox17b.2 with indistinguishable activities and identical expression in presumptive vegetal endoderm cells of gastrula embryos.
source: In Xenopus tropicalis, there are three redundant genes: sox17a, sox17b.1 and sox17b.2 (collectively sox17) with indistinguishable activities and identical expression in presumptive vegetal endoderm cells of gastrula embryos (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A; D'Souza et al., 2003; Hellsten et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Microinjection of a combination of antisense morpholino oligos targeting all three sox17 paralogs resulted in a robust knockdown of Sox17 protein.
source: Microinjection of a combination of antisense morpholino oligos (sox17aMO and sox17bMO) targeting all three paralogs resulted in a robust knockdown of Sox17 protein as confirmed by immunostaining (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The Sox17-MO phenotype was consistent with previous reports and phenocopied mouse mutants with defective gut development.
source: The Sox17-MO phenotype was consistent with previous reports (Clements et al., 2003; Sinner et al., 2006) and phenocopied mouse mutants with defective gut development (Kanai-Azuma et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Injection of mRNA encoding mouse Sox17 rescued both the anatomical and gene expression phenotypes confirming the efficacy and specificity of the MOs.
source: Injection of mRNA encoding mouse Sox17 rescued both the anatomical and gene expression phenotypes confirming the efficacy and specificity of the MOs (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Differential expression analysis of control-MO and Sox17-MO embryos identified 1023 Sox17-regulated genes (>2 fold change, FDR< 5%).
source: Differential expression analysis of control-MO and Sox17-MO embryos identified 1023 Sox17-regulated genes (>2 fold change, FDR< 5%) (Figure 1D and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: 493 transcripts were downregulated in Sox17-depleted embryos and 530 transcript were upregulated.
source: In total, 493 transcripts were downregulated in Sox17-depleted embryos and 530 transcript were upregulated.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: >75% of the differentially expressed genes were changed by Sox17 depletion during the mid-late gastrula (NF10.5–12).
source: The time course data revealed that >75% of the differentially expressed genes were changed by Sox17 depletion (either directly or indirectly) during the mid-late gastrula (NF10.5–12), consistent with a role in maintaining endodermal fate after initial induction by Nodal signaling in the blastula (NF9) (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on time course RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Differentially expressed genes include 73 TFs, including known Sox17 targets foxa2 and hnf1b.
source: Differentially expressed genes include 73 TFs, including known Sox17 targets foxa2 and hnf1b (Sinner et al., 2004; Sinner et al., 2006), and paracrine signaling components (Supplementary file 1) such as the Hedgehog pathway (dhh, hhip, gli1); a key epithelial signal in gut organogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Over 30% of the genes upregulated early (NF9-10) in the Sox17-depleted embryos were normally enriched in the ectoderm or mesoderm tissue.
source: Interestingly, over 30% of the genes upregulated early (NF9-10) in the Sox17-depleted embryos were normally enriched in the ectoderm or mesoderm tissue; examples include ectoderm-promoting TFs tfap2a and lhx5 (Houston and Wylie, 2003; Figure 1D–F) as well as the mesoderm TFs foxf1, tbx20 and hlx.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis and comparison to spatial expression data.

claim: Sox17 plays an important role in repressing ectoderm and mesoderm fate in vegetal endoderm cells.
source: This suggests that Sox17 plays an important role in repressing ectoderm and mesoderm fate in vegetal endoderm cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the Results section based on the observation that ectoderm and mesoderm genes are upregulated in Sox17-depleted embryos.

claim: Sox17 negatively regulated ~150 genes that are normally enriched in the vegetal endoderm and dorsal mesendoderm.
source: Unexpectedly Sox17 also negatively regulated ~150 genes that are normally enriched in the vegetal endoderm and dorsal mesendoderm.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis and comparison to spatial expression data.

claim: Sox17 acts as a negative feedback inhibitor that restricts excessive endoderm development by restraining Nodal activity after initial induction.
source: These data indicate that Sox17 acts as a negative feedback inhibitor that restricts excessive endoderm development by restraining Nodal activity after initial induction.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the Results section based on the observation that Nodal pathway genes are upregulated in Sox17-depleted embryos.

claim: Sox17 ChIP-seq in gastrula (NF10.5) embryos identified 8436 statistically significant Sox17-bound putative CRMs (IDR; p<0.05).
source: To identify direct Sox17 targets we generated and validated anti-Sox17 antibodies (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C) and performed Sox17 ChIP-seq in gastrula (NF10.5) embryos, identifying 8436 statistically significant Sox17-bound putative CRMs (IDR; p<0.05) (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: Sox17-bound CRMs were associated with 4801 genes.
source: These were associated with 4801 genes (Figure 2A), based on annotation to the nearest transcription start-site (TSS) by HOMER (Heinz et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on ChIP-seq analysis and annotation.

claim: 88% of Sox17-bound loci were in introns or intergenic regions more than 1 kb away from the TSS, consistent with Sox17 binding at distal CRMs.
source: 88% of Sox17-bound loci were in introns or intergenic regions more than 1 kb away from the TSS, consistent with Sox17 binding at distal CRMs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: Most of the Sox17-bound genomic loci were also bound by Ep300, indicative of active enhancers.
source: A comparison to published ChIP-seq data of Xenopus embryos at the same stage (Hontelez et al., 2015) showed that most of the Sox17-bound genomic loci were also bound by Ep300, (Figure 2B,E) indicative of active enhancers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on comparison to published ChIP-seq data.

claim: Motif analysis of the ChIP-seq peaks confirmed that Sox17 motifs were the most enriched.
source: Motif analysis of the ChIP-seq peaks confirmed that Sox17 motifs were the most enriched, as expected (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on motif analysis of ChIP-seq data.

claim: Control ChIP-qPCR experiments of Sox17-MO embryos showed binding reduced to near background levels at 9 of 10 loci tested confirming a robust knockdown and the specificity of the Sox17 antibody.
source: Control ChIP-qPCR experiments of Sox17-MO embryos showed binding reduced to near background levels at 9 of 10 loci tested confirming a robust knockdown and the specificity of the Sox17 antibody (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on ChIP-qPCR validation experiments.

claim: Intersecting the RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data identified 315 genes associated with 609 Sox17-bound enhancers, which are likely to be direct transcriptional targets.
source: Intersecting the RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data identified 315 genes associated with 609 Sox17-bound enhancers, which are likely to be direct transcriptional targets (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: Of the Sox17-bound and regulated genes, 197 genes (383 peaks) were positively regulated by Sox17.
source: Of the Sox17-bound and regulated genes, 197 genes (383 peaks) were positively regulated by Sox17 (down in Sox17MOs) including slc5a8, hnf1b, foxa1 and dhh (Figure 2E), all of which were previously suggested to be direct Sox17-targets.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: Sox17 negatively regulated 118 putative direct targets including ectodermal genes, endoderm-enriched Nodal pathway genes and Wnt-regulated organizer genes.
source: Sox17 negatively regulated 118 putative direct targets (up in Sox17MOs) including ectodermal genes (lhx5, foxi2 and tfap2a), endoderm-enriched Nodal pathway genes (nodal1, gdf3, gdf6 and mix1) and Wnt-regulated organizer genes (dkk and fst), suggesting direct transcriptional repression (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: ~45% of peaks associated with Sox17-activated genes were also enriched for LIM-homeodomain binding sites.
source: Interestingly, ~45% of peaks associated with Sox17-activated genes were also enriched for LIM-homeodomain binding sites, in contrast to peaks from Sox17-repressed genes which were enriched for Tbx or Pou motifs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on motif analysis of ChIP-seq data.

claim: Sox17 may coordinately engage enhancers with other core endoderm GRN TFs and mediate activation or repression of target genes depending on the interacting TFs.
source: This suggests that Sox17 may coordinately engage enhancers with other core endoderm GRN TFs and mediate activation or repression of target genes depending on the interacting TFs.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the Results section based on motif analysis showing enrichment of different TF binding sites in activated vs repressed genes.

claim: RNA-seq of control-MO and Bcat-MO depleted embryos identified a total of 2568 Bcat-regulated genes (>2 fold change, FDR < 5%).
source: RNA-seq of control-MO and Bcat-MO depleted embryos at eight time points from blastula and gastrula stages (NF7-12) identified a total of 2568 Bcat-regulated genes (>2 fold change, FDR < 5%), 1321 of which were downregulated and 1247 upregulated in the Bcat-MO embryos (Figure 3A and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: 1321 genes were downregulated and 1247 upregulated in the Bcat-MO embryos.
source: RNA-seq of control-MO and Bcat-MO depleted embryos at eight time points from blastula and gastrula stages (NF7-12) identified a total of 2568 Bcat-regulated genes (>2 fold change, FDR < 5%), 1321 of which were downregulated and 1247 upregulated in the Bcat-MO embryos (Figure 3A and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: The Bcat-dependent genes encoded 251 TFs, (~20% of all the TFs in the genome).
source: Remarkably, the Bcat-dependent genes encoded 251 TFs, (~20% of all the TFs in the genome), reinforcing the notion that Wnt/Bcat initiates a transcriptional cascade in the early embryo.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on RNA-seq analysis.

claim: Intersecting the Bcat-MO RNA-seq data with previously published Bcat ChIP-seq data identified 898 putative direct target genes associated with 2616 Bcat-bound CRMs.
source: Intersecting the Bcat-MO RNA-seq data with previously published Bcat ChIP-seq data from Xenopus tropicalis gastrula (Nakamura et al., 2016) identified 898 putative direct target genes associated with 2616 Bcat-bound CRMs (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq and published ChIP-seq data.

claim: In the Bcat-MO, 546 genes were downregulated, and 352 genes had increased expression.
source: In the Bcat-MO, 546 genes were downregulated , and 352 genes had increased expression in Bcat-MO embryos (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: Almost 200 Bcat-bound and -regulated genes had endoderm enriched expression including most of the core endoderm TFs.
source: Most importantly, almost 200 Bcat-bound and -regulated genes had endoderm enriched expression including most of the core endoderm TFs; sox17, foxa, eomes, gata4, mix1 and mixer (Figure 3D and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, and spatial expression data.

claim: Wnt/Bcat directly regulates the transcription of many endodermal genes, contrary to the prevailing view that Bcat promotes endoderm fate primarily by activating Nodal ligand expression.
source: Thus, contrary to the prevailing view that Bcat promotes endoderm fate primarily by activating Nodal ligand expression (Blythe et al., 2010; Hyde and Old, 2000), we find that Wnt/Bcat also directly regulates the transcription of many endodermal genes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the observation that many endoderm genes are directly bound and regulated by Bcat.

claim: De novo motif analysis showed that the Bcat-bound peaks were more enriched for Sox than canonical Tcf motifs, 2nd versus 5th ranked, respectively.
source: Surprisingly, de novo motif analysis showed that the Bcat-bound peaks were more enriched for Sox than canonical Tcf motifs, 2nd versus 5th ranked, respectively (Figure 3C; Nakamura et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on motif analysis of ChIP-seq data.

claim: Analysis of other previously published Bcat ChIP-Seq datasets in X. tropicalis gastrula embryos and Flag-tagged Bcat ChIP-Seq in X. laevis gastrula also report a high enrichment for Sox and Tcf motifs.
source: Consistent with this, analysis of other previously published Bcat ChIP-Seq datsets in X. tropicalis gastrula embryos (Gentsch et al., 2019) and Flag-tagged Bcat ChIP-Seq in X. laevis gastrula (Kjolby and Harland, 2017) also report a high enrichment for Sox and Tcf motifs (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis of published ChIP-seq data.

claim: 3956 genomic loci are co-occupied by both Sox17 and Bcat, and these had epigenetic signatures of active enhancers.
source: Intersection of the ChIP-seq datasets identified 3956 genomic loci co-occupied by both Sox17 and Bcat, and these had epigenetic signatures of active enhancers (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the Results section based on integration of ChIP-seq datasets.

claim: 3956 co-occupied loci represent a third of all Sox17 genomic binding in the gastrula.
source: This represents a third of all Sox17 genomic binding in the gastrula.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on ChIP-seq analysis.

claim: 415 transcripts were regulated by both Sox17 and Bcat, comprising of ~40% of the Sox17-regulated and ~15% of the Bcat-regulated transcriptome.
source: Comparison of the Sox17-MO and Bcat-MO RNA-seq datasets identified 415 transcripts that were regulated by both Sox17 and Bcat; comprising of ~40% of the Sox17-regulated and ~15% of the Bcat-regulated transcriptome (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq datasets.

claim: Co-regulation with Wnt/Bcat is a major feature of the Sox17-regulated endoderm GRN.
source: This suggests that co-regulation with Wnt/Bcat is a major feature of the Sox17-regulated endoderm GRN.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the Results section based on the extensive overlap between Sox17 and Bcat genomic binding and regulation.

claim: 84 genes (191 Peaks) were bound and regulated by both Sox17 and Bcat.
source: In total, 84 genes (191 Peaks) were bound and regulated by both Sox17 and Bcat (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: 53% (101/191) of the co-bound and coregulated peaks contained both Sox17 and Tcf DNA-binding motifs compared to 31% in background genomic sequences.
source: A comprehensive motif analysis of the 191 co-bound and coregulated peaks using the CIS-BP database (Lambert et al., 2019) revealed that 53% (101/191) of the peaks contained both Sox17 and Tcf DNA-binding motifs (e.g. dkk1, lhx5 and osr1) compared to 31% in background genomic sequences (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E and Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on motif analysis of ChIP-seq data.

claim: 24% (46/191) of the co-bound and coregulated peaks had Sox motifs but no Tcf sites, suggesting that Bcat might be recruited to these loci independent of Tcfs.
source: In contrast 24% (46/191) of the peaks had Sox motifs but no Tcf sites (e.g. six1), suggesting that Bcat might be recruited to these loci independent of Tcfs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on motif analysis of ChIP-seq data.

claim: ChIP-reChIP experiments demonstrated that Sox17 and Bcat bound the same enhancers in the same cells.
source: To test whether Sox17 and Bcat bound the same enhancers in the same cells we performed ChIP-reChIP experiments. First anti-Bcat ChIP was performed on 500 gastrulae. DNA eluted from the first ChIP was then re-precipitated with either anti-Sox17 or a negative control IgG antibody. All four loci tested by ChIP-reChIP qPCR (six1, dkk1, lhx5 and gli1) showed enrichment compared to IgG demonstrating that these genomic loci (~150 bp in length) were simultaneously bound by Sox17 and Bcat in endodermal cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on ChIP-reChIP experiments.

claim: 32/84 co-bound and coregulated genes were activated by both Sox17 and Bcat and tended to have endoderm enriched expression.
source: The 84 co-bound and coregulated genes fell into four regulatory categories (Figure 4C,E); 32/84 were activated by both Sox17 and Bcat (e.g. six1 and osr1) and tended to have endoderm enriched expression
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, and spatial expression data.

claim: 27/84 co-bound and coregulated genes were activated by Bcat but repressed by Sox17 and tended to be enriched in the organizer mesendoderm.
source: 27/84 were activated by Bcat but repressed by Sox17 (e.g. dkk1) and these tended to be enriched in the organizer mesendoderm
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, and spatial expression data.

claim: 19/84 co-bound and coregulated genes were positively regulated by Sox17 and negatively regulated by Bcat.
source: 19/84 were positively regulated by Sox17 and negatively regulated by Bcat (up in the Bcat MO)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: 6/84 co-bound and coregulated genes were negatively regulated by both Sox17 and Bcat.
source: and finally 6/84 were negatively regulated by both Sox17 and Bcat.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: Bcat positively regulated most of the co-bound and coregulated genes (59/84, 70%).
source: The observation that Bcat positively regulated most of these genes (59/84, 70%) was consistent with its known role in transcriptional activation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: Sox17 positively regulated 60% of co-bound and coregulated targets and repressed 40% of targets, suggesting context-dependent activity.
source: Sox17 positively regulated 60% of targets and repressed 40% of targets, suggesting context-dependent activity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data.

claim: Co-injection of mSox17 mRNA could not rescue the normal expression patterns of six1, osr1, lhx5 or dkk1 in Bcat-MO embryos, demonstrating that reduced Sox17 in Bcat-depleted embryos cannot account for the disrupted expression.
source: Co-injection of mSox17 mRNA could not rescue the normal expression patterns of six1, osr1, lhx5 or dkk1 in Bcat-MO embryos, but it did rescue foxa1 expression (Figure 5). This demonstrates that reduced Sox17 in Bcat-depleted embryos cannot account for the disrupted six1, osr1, lhx5 or dkk1 expression, but it can account for the reduced foxa1 expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on epistasis experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Co-injection of stabilized (ca)Bcat mRNA rescued the normal expression of foxa1 but not six1, osr1, lhx5 or dkk1 in Sox17-morphants indicating that the defects in their expression were not simply due to reduced Wnt signaling.
source: Similarly, co-injection of stabilized (ca)Bcat mRNA rescued the normal expression of foxa1 but not six1, osr1, lhx5 or dkk1 in Sox17-morphants indicating that the defects in their expression were not simply due to reduced Wnt signaling (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on epistasis experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Sox17 and Bcat coordinate spatial gene expression in the embryo in a complex gene-specific manner.
source: These experiments also show that Sox17 and Bcat coordinate spatial gene expression in the embryo in a complex gene-specific manner.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the Results section based on epistasis experiments.

claim: The −1 kb six1 enhancer is evolutionarily conserved from Xenopus to human containing three Sox-binding sites but no predicted Tcf-binding sites.
source: The −1 kb six1 enhancer is evolutionarily conserved from Xenopus to human containing three Sox-binding sites but no predicted Tcf-binding sites (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on sequence analysis.

claim: In mouse, the −1 kb six1 enhancer can drive transgenic expression in the embryonic gut tube.
source: In mouse, this enhancer can drive transgenic expression in the embryonic gut tube, although the TFs that modulate it were previously unknown (Sato et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The human SIX1 CRM is also bound by SOX17 in human PSC-derived endoderm.
source: Analysis of published ChIP-seq data indicate that, like in Xenopus, the human SIX1 CRM is also bound by SOX17 in human PSC-derived endoderm (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A; Tsankov et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on analysis of published ChIP-seq data.

claim: Both Sox17 and Bcat are required for activation of the −1 kb six1 enhancer.
source: Depletion of endogenous Sox17 or Bcat abolished expression of the −1six1:luc reporter and this was rescued by adding back mSox17 to Sox17-MO or by adding back caBcat mRNA to Bcat-MO embryos (Figure 6C). However, co-injection of mSox17 could not rescue expression in Bcat-MO embryos and nor could caBcat RNA rescue expression in Sox17-MOs (Figure 6C). These epistasis experiments indicate that both Sox17 and Bcat are required for activation of the −1 kb six1 enhancer.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays.

claim: Sox17 restricts Bcat-mediated transactivation at the dkk1 and lhx5 enhancers.
source: In contrast, in the case of the −1.6 kb dkk1, −7.5 kb dkk1 and the −1 kb lhx5:luc constructs, depletion of Bcat abrogated reporter activity, whereas Sox17 depletion resulted in significantly elevated reporter activity, indicating that Sox17 restricts Bcat-mediated transactivation at the dkk1 and lhx5 enhancers (Figure 6E, and Figure 6—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays.

claim: Injection of mSox17 but not caBcat mRNA was sufficient to stimulate the −1 kb six1:luc and human SIX1:luc reporters in the ectoderm, but co-injection of caBcat along with mSox17 synergistically activated the reporters.
source: Injection of mSox17 but not caBcat mRNA was sufficient to stimulate the −1 kb six1:luc and human SIX1:luc reporters in the ectoderm, but co-injection of caBcat along with mSox17 synergistically activated the reporters (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays.

claim: caBcat but not mSox17 was able to activate the dkk1 and lhx5 reporters in ventral ectoderm, and co-injection of mSox17 suppressed the ability of caBcat to stimulate these reporters.
source: On the other hand, caBcat but not mSox17 was able to activate the dkk1 and lhx5 reporters in ventral ectoderm, and co-injection of mSox17 suppressed the ability of caBcat to stimulate these reporters (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 2C,D), consistent with the endogenous regulation (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays.

claim: The ability of Sox17 to activate the six1 reporter or suppress Bcat-induced activation of the dkk1 and lhx5 reporters required the DNA-binding function of Sox17.
source: The ability of Sox17 to activate the six1 reporter or suppress Bcat-induced activation of the dkk1 and lhx5 reporters required the DNA-binding function of Sox17. A M76A point mutation in mSox17, known to disrupt the DNA-binding HMG domain (Sinner et al., 2007) significantly reduced Sox17's ability to activate the six1 or repress the dkk1 reporter activity, respectively (Figure 6C,E and Figure 6—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays with mutant Sox17.

claim: Tcf7l1-VP16 fusion construct had little to no impact on the six1 reporter, but robustly activated the dkk1 and lhx5 reporters in ventral ectoderm.
source: To test whether or not Tcfs regulate these enhancers, we injected a Tcf7l1-VP16 fusion construct which constitutively activates Tcf-target gene transcription (Darken and Wilson, 2001). This had little to no impact on the six1 reporter, but robustly activated the dkk1 and lhx5 reporters in ventral ectoderm (Figure 6D,F and Figure 6—figure supplement 2D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays.

claim: Loss of the Sox17 sites abolished normal and Sox17/Bcat-induced expression of the six1:luc reporter.
source: We next mutated the Sox17 and Tcf-binding sites in the six1 and dkk1 enhancers and examined the impact on Sox17, Bcat and Tcf regulation. Loss of the Sox17 sites abolished normal and Sox17/Bcat-induced expression of the six1:luc reporter (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays with mutant enhancers.

claim: Mutation of the Sox sites in the dkk1 enhancers resulted in elevated reporter activity consistent with Sox17-mediated repression.
source: In contrast, mutation of the Sox sites in the dkk1 enhancers resulted in elevated reporter activity consistent with Sox17-mediated repression (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays with mutant enhancers.

claim: Deletion of the Tcf sites in the dkk1 enhancers abolished expression in the dorsal mesendoderm as well as Bcat or Tcf7l1-VP16-induced activation in the ventral ectoderm, consistent with Bcat-Tcf complexes activating these enhancers.
source: Deletion of the Tcf sites in the dkk1 enhancers abolished expression in the dorsal mesendoderm as well as Bcat or Tcf7l1-VP16-induced activation in the ventral ectoderm, consistent with Bcat-Tcf complexes activating these enhancers (Figure 6F and Figure 6—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays with mutant enhancers.

claim: An osr1 enhancer +7 kb downstream of its TSS and a +3 kb igf3 enhancer have no evidence of Tcf binding sites and were both synergistically activated by Sox17 and Bcat, whereas co-injection of Tcf7l1-VP16 failed to activate either reporter.
source: To examine the generality of the apparent Tcf-independent regulation of six1, we identified two additional enhancers with similar characteristics: an osr1 enhancer +7 kb downstream of its TSS (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B) and a +3 kb igf3 enhancer (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C and Supplementary file 6). Both these enhancers have no evidence of Tcf binding sites and they were both synergistically activated by Sox17 and Bcat, whereas co-injection of Tcf7l1-VP16 failed to activate either reporter (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays.

claim: Sox17 and Bcat synergistically can activate the six, osr1 and igf3 enhancers, likely independent of Tcfs.
source: From these collective data, we conclude that Sox17 and Bcat synergistically can activate the six, osr1 and igf3 enhancers, likely independent of Tcfs.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays.

claim: The dkk1 and lhx5 enhancers are activated through a Bcat/Tcf transcription mechanism, with Sox17 spatially restricting Bcat/Tcf activity to maintain cell-type-specific gene expression.
source: In contrast, the dkk1 and lhx5 enhancers are activated through a Bcat/Tcf transcription mechanism, with Sox17 spatially restricting Bcat/Tcf activity to maintain cell-type-specific gene expression (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on luciferase reporter assays.

claim: In all vertebrate embryos, Sox17 is specifically expressed in the gastrula endoderm where it is required for early gut development.
source: In all vertebrate embryos, Sox17 is specifically expressed in the gastrula endoderm where it is required for early gut development (Clements et al., 2003; Hudson et al., 1997; Kanai-Azuma et al., 2002; Viotti et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Only few direct transcriptional targets of Sox17 have been identified (e.g.: hnf1b, foxa1 and dhh).
source: Despite the critical role of Sox17 in endoderm development, only few of its direct transcriptional targets have been identified (e.g.: hnf1b, foxa1 and dhh) (Ahmed et al., 2004; Sinner et al., 2004; Yagi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In Xenopus, ectopic Sox17 is sufficient to initiate endoderm development in pluripotent blastula animal cap cells.
source: In Xenopus, ectopic Sox17 is sufficient to initiate endoderm development in pluripotent blastula animal cap cells (Clements et al., 2003; Hudson et al., 1997), and co-injection of stabilized Bcat can enhance this activity (Sinner et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Co-injection of stabilized Bcat can enhance Sox17's ability to initiate endoderm development in animal cap cells.
source: In Xenopus, ectopic Sox17 is sufficient to initiate endoderm development in pluripotent blastula animal cap cells (Clements et al., 2003; Hudson et al., 1997), and co-injection of stabilized Bcat can enhance this activity (Sinner et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Sox17 can physically interact with Bcat in vitro.
source: Sox17 can physically interact with Bcat in vitro and suppress the transcriptional activity of generic Tcf/Bcat reporter constructs (TOPflash) in tissue culture experiments (Sinner et al., 2007; Zorn et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Sox17 can suppress the transcriptional activity of generic Tcf/Bcat reporter constructs (TOPflash) in tissue culture experiments.
source: Sox17 can physically interact with Bcat in vitro and suppress the transcriptional activity of generic Tcf/Bcat reporter constructs (TOPflash) in tissue culture experiments (Sinner et al., 2007; Zorn et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: 20% of the Xenopus Sox17-bound genes were also SOX17-bound in hPSC-induced definitive endoderm.
source: A comparison to published human ChIP-Seq data revealed that 20% of the Xenopus Sox17-bound genes were also SOX17-bound in hPSC-induced definitive endoderm (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D; Tsankov et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on comparison to published ChIP-seq data.

claim: GO analysis of the conserved SOX17-bound genes show an enrichment for 'Tgfb receptor activity' and 'Bcat binding'.
source: GO analysis of the conserved SOX17-bound genes show an enrichment for 'Tgfb receptor activity' and 'Bcat binding' (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E), reinforcing the notion that functional interaction with the Nodal and Wnt pathways is a conserved feature of the Sox17-regulated endoderm GRN.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on GO analysis of conserved Sox17-bound genes.

claim: Functional interaction with the Nodal and Wnt pathways is a conserved feature of the Sox17-regulated endoderm GRN.
source: GO analysis of the conserved SOX17-bound genes show an enrichment for 'Tgfb receptor activity' and 'Bcat binding' (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E), reinforcing the notion that functional interaction with the Nodal and Wnt pathways is a conserved feature of the Sox17-regulated endoderm GRN.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the Results section based on GO analysis of conserved Sox17-bound genes.

claim: Sox17 sits atop of the regulatory hierarchy regulating endoderm differentiation.
source: This confirms that Sox17 sits atop of the regulatory hierarchy regulating endoderm differentiation.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the Results section based on the observation that Sox17 regulates many TFs and signaling components.

claim: Sox17 acts in a negative feedback loop to restrain Nodal signaling.
source: We demonstrate that functional interactions with canonical Wnt signaling is a key feature of the Sox17-regulated GRN. Over a third of all Bcat and Sox17 genomic binding in the gastrula occur at the same CRMs. In some instances, Sox17 suppresses Bcat-Tcf mediated transcription, while in other cases, Sox17 and Bcat synergistically activates enhancers apparently independently of Tcfs, indicating a novel mode of regulation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding.

claim: In embryos and pluripotent stem cells (PSCs), Nodal/Smad2 and Wnt/ß-catenin signaling cooperate to initiate the mesendoderm program and subsequent development of definitive endoderm progenitors.
source: In embryos and pluripotent stem cells (PSCs), Nodal/Smad2 and Wnt/ß-catenin (Ctnnb1; hereafter Bcat) signaling cooperate to initiate the mesendoderm program and subsequent development of definitive endoderm progenitors, which gives rise to the epithelia of the digestive and respiratory systems (Sumi et al., 2008; Zorn and Wells, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A core set of endoderm TFs: Sox17, Gata4-6, Eomes, Foxa1/2 and Mix family of homeodomain TFs execute the endoderm GRN.
source: Downstream of Nodal and Wnt, a core set of endoderm TFs: Sox17, Gata4-6, Eomes, Foxa1/2 and Mix family of homeodomain TFs execute the endoderm GRN (Arnold et al., 2008; Charney et al., 2017b; Engert et al., 2013; Sinner et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In Xenopus, maternal Wnt/Bcat, active on the dorsal side of the blastula, is required for high levels of nodal expression at the onset of zygotic transcription.
source: In Xenopus where endoderm specification is well studied, the Nodal and Wnt pathways interact at several levels. First, maternal (m) Wnt/Bcat, active on the dorsal side of the blastula, is required for high levels of nodal expression at the onset of zygotic transcription (Hyde and Old, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Nodal and mWnt cooperate to promote the expression of endoderm TFs Sox17, Foxa2 and many dorsal mesendoderm organizer genes.
source: Then Nodal and mWnt cooperate to promote the expression of endoderm TFs Sox17, Foxa2 and many dorsal mesendoderm organizer genes (Xanthos et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Zygotic wnt8 is expressed on the ventral side of the gastrula where, together with Nodal signaling, it promotes ventral and posterior mesendoderm identities.
source: A few hours later, zygotic (z) wnt8 (a Nodal target) is expressed on the ventral side of the gastrula where, together with Nodal signaling, it promotes ventral and posterior mesendoderm identities (Charney et al., 2017b; Stevens et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In mammals, early Wnt/Bcat activates expression of Nodal and core endoderm TFs, with prolonged Wnt promoting posterior hindgut fate.
source: In mammals, early Wnt/Bcat similarly activates expression of Nodal and core endoderm TFs, with prolonged Wnt promoting posterior hindgut fate (Engert et al., 2013; Zorn and Wells, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: All Tcfs have nearly identical DNA-binding specificities.
source: How distinct context-specific Wnt target genes are selected is unclear since all Tcfs have nearly identical DNA-binding specificities (Badis et al., 2009; Ramakrishnan and Cadigan, 2017) and for the most part they are ubiquitously expressed.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The Wnt-enhanceosome interacts with other lineage-specific TFs to integrate lineage-specific inputs.
source: An emerging idea is that the Wnt-enhanceosome also interacts with other lineage-specific TFs to integrate lineage-specific inputs (Gammons and Bienz, 2018; Trompouki et al., 2011); yet, how these impact genomic specificity in vivo is largely untested and the idea of Tcf-independent Wnt-mediated transcription remains controversial.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Sox17 establishes Sox17 as a tissue-specific modifier of Wnt responses.
source: Our findings establish Sox17 as a tissue-specific modifier of Wnt responses and point to a novel paradigm where genomic specificity of Wnt/β-catenin transcription is determined through functional interactions between lineage-specific Sox TFs and β-catenin/Tcf transcriptional complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary conclusion of the study.

claim: Genomic specificity of Wnt/β-catenin transcription is determined through functional interactions between lineage-specific Sox TFs and β-catenin/Tcf transcriptional complexes.
source: Our findings establish Sox17 as a tissue-specific modifier of Wnt responses and point to a novel paradigm where genomic specificity of Wnt/β-catenin transcription is determined through functional interactions between lineage-specific Sox TFs and β-catenin/Tcf transcriptional complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary conclusion of the study.

claim: This mechanism has important implications across a diverse range of developmental and disease contexts given the ubiquitous nature of Sox TFs and Wnt signaling.
source: Given the ubiquitous nature of Sox TFs and Wnt signaling, this mechanism has important implications across a diverse range of developmental and disease contexts.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a broader implication of the findings.
